f1_gs_1000.hint: g = h − Ts with T in kelvin.

f1_gl_1100.hint: Use the LIQUID row: g = h − Ts with T in kelvin.

f1_crossing.hint: Collect the T terms on one side and the constants on the other, then divide.

f1_gmix_025.hint: Weight each phase's g at 900 K by its fraction and add the two.

f1_best_fl_900.hint: Does g_mix rise or fall as f_L grows at 900 K? Then choose the end of the allowed range 0 ≤ f_L ≤ 1 with the lower g_mix.

f1_gs_1050.hint: Use the SOLID row: g = h − Ts at the new temperature.

f1_gl_1050.hint: Use the LIQUID row: g = h − Ts at the new temperature.

f1_min_1050.hint: Take the lower of your two energies.

f1_report_a.hint: Recompute g_S at 900 K from the model, and put both energies in the same unit before comparing.

f1_report_b_sum.hint: Add the two reported fractions as they stand.

f1_report_b_balanced.hint: One mole needs f_S + f_L = 1 exactly. Rescaling the reported fractions would silently change the reported state.
